question.problem:
The vectors $\textbf{a},$ $\textbf{b},$ and $\textbf{c}$ are shown in the diagram below. Find $\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}-\textbf{c}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/9665262608454d38d6a442715345cc014d40ca2e3d9a7cdf7c8cd0b8fc00f0d7.png)
question.worked_solution:
First, we use the triangle law of addition to find 

$$
\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}.
$$

The resultant $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ is the vector that joins the tail of $\textbf{a}$ and the head of $\textbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/2643b94a575f1b2cd9967e530019b8b100928b2f9888aaf833dd84423fbe6e10.png)

Now, we use the triangle law of addition to find 

$$
(\textbf{a}+\textbf{b})+(-\textbf{c}).
$$

We draw $-\textbf{c}$ from the head of $\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}.$ So, we have the vector that goes from the tail of $\textbf{a}$ to the head of $-\textbf{c}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/d77ad19b87fe8afba44663482ed6e8adfb2f251c4439c488ab7b3cde8b4a60ac.png)
